title: The served default on JevBench's published items and four Decision Index benchmarks, one card, internal
hardware: 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (96 GB)

software.patch_series_flag_note: the flag was named VLLM_R9_SUFFIX_STAGING when this run was made; its logs keep that name

serving.requests: one at a time, every question distinct (the Decision Index board rule)

code.state: the private repository's served code of 2026-09-27, before the rendering rules, the tie-break rule and the global temperature
code.public_equivalent: python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine --model-class view --no-hide-index-keys --no-desnake-labels --temperature 1 [--orders 2]; the tie-break then was the first maximum in wire order (now the key that sorts first), which changes a choice only on exact ties

arms.two_orders: --orders 2 (two-order averaging after Reflex; the branch disagreement per item in disagreement_two_orders.json)

harnesses.jevbench: github.com/fstandhartinger/jevbench @ d06ee95, typesafe adapter, the harness's own summarize; the 231 published items (easy 48, original 72, hard 111)
harnesses.decision_index: github.com/apolinario/decision-index @ 87d4650, edition 0.2.1, http engine, the kit's own score; rows rebuilt with `suite rebuild --only 4 5 21 25 57` (BANKING77 3,080, CLINC150+OOS 5,500, GPQA Diamond 198, MMLU-Pro 12,032 at TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro@b189ec7)

results.note: private readings: JevBench's official score needs its sealed set, and a Decision Index value needs all 38 benchmarks; neither is claimed

files.jevbench/<arm>/<file>/: the harness's results.jsonl (per item), summary.json and manifest.json
files.decision_index/<arm>/items.jsonl.gz: per request: ids, the payload's sha256, our response, timings (the payload itself removed)
files.decision_index/<arm>/: the kit's benchmark-summary.json and our di_report.json (decisio.bench.di_report), environment.json, status.json
files.disagreement_two_orders.json: per item: board, set, id, the two orders' disagreement, correct with two orders and with one
files.conformance.json: C2-C4 (decisio.serve.systemone_conformance); C3 and C4 rows carry the private suite's task and index, not its text
files.gates.log: the C1 serving gates' result lines (tests/gpu/serving_gates.py); G4 used a private LoRA adapter
files.health_<arm>.json: the server's /health at the start of each arm

excluded: item text of any benchmark (Decision Index payloads, JevBench raw requests and responses)
Jev's published board figures, and any Jev output
vLLM start-up logs, box logs and addresses
the same-item comparison with our own item sets (it includes Jev's answers)
the contamination screen (it names private training files)
